brief: Goldman's Q3 Hedge Fund Trend Monitor (Ben Snider) finds funds cut AI exposure and rotated into cyclicals and defensives, but it did not help: the VIP basket of top hedge fund longs, 0.9-correlated with AI, semis and memory baskets, underperformed the S&P by 14pp over six months, matching the worst stretches since 2008 and 2022. Funds cut net leverage to five-year lows (42%, or 48.2% beta-adjusted) while pushing Financials, Consumer Discretionary, Industrials, Staples and Utilities to 10-year-high tilts. Goldman's Louis Miller argues this rotation recreates the 4Q'18 setup: high-beta cyclicals, lending-sensitive stocks and European consumer baskets were the hardest-hit pockets that cycle, and are now crowded again at richer valuations (15x forward earnings, a 40% premium to the 2018 trough). Mutual funds, meanwhile, sit on record-low cash and high beta (1.38x, near the 2022 peak) and have not de-risked, leaving them as the likely sellers if the analog plays out. Miller's conclusion: funds may have swapped one crowded trade for another. His preferred longs are a high-vs-low free-cash-flow pair, selective Healthcare over Staples, and a tail hedge roughly 2.5% from its trigger.
